title: A multi-day climb on Glacier Peak
summary: A Mountaineers team traveled through White Pass and Glacier Gap on a multi-day Glacier Peak climb. Their report describes camp choices, changing weather, snow travel and the practical details that shape a long alpine outing.
takeaway: Thoughtful camp selection, water planning and adapting to changing mountain conditions supported the team's multi-day objective.
sourceLabel: The Mountaineers - Glacier Peak trip report
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of snow-covered alpine peaks

title: A glacier traverse with a safer turnaround
summary: A Mountaineers team set out on the Inspiration-McAllister-Klawatti Ice Cap traverse, managing a difficult approach and several days of glacier travel. As fatigue and illness affected the group, they shortened the traverse rather than press on.
takeaway: The team treated a conservative change of plan as a successful outcome, prioritizing group health and sound judgment over completing the original route.
sourceLabel: The Mountaineers - Ice Cap traverse report
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of a high mountain lake and surrounding peaks

title: A careful overnight climb of Sloan Peak
summary: A Mountaineers group camped below Sloan Peak, reviewed the next day's plan together and adjusted it after checking snow, water and ridge conditions. The team continued over the glacier and reached the summit before breakfast.
takeaway: A shared briefing and willingness to adjust camp and start plans helped the group respond to current conditions on the route.
sourceLabel: The Mountaineers - Sloan Peak trip report
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of a climber on steep mountain terrain

title: Four days in the Mount Margaret Backcountry
location: Mount St. Helens, Washington, United States
summary: A Mountaineers group spent four days traveling and camping in the Mount Margaret Backcountry. The trip report follows the route through volcanic history, recovering landscapes, wildflower meadows and nights at established camps.
takeaway: A multi-day camp can combine route planning, shared time outdoors and learning about the landscape without making a summit the measure of success.
sourceLabel: The Mountaineers - Mount Margaret trip report
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of a mountain valley in morning light

title: A hut-to-hut journey from Mont Blanc to the Matterhorn
location: Walker’s Haute Route, France and Switzerland
summary: A Mountaineers Global Adventures group traveled the Walker’s Haute Route between Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn. Its trip report shares daily observations from the long hut-to-hut journey through the Alps.
takeaway: Organized hut-to-hut travel connects daily route decisions, shared logistics and a sustained team effort across a multi-week mountain journey.
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of a mountain summit beneath a starry sky

title: A scramble that included helping another hiker
location: Vesper and Wolf Peaks, Washington, United States
summary: A Mountaineers group completed a Vesper and Wolf Peaks scramble, then helped a lost hiker reconnect with their friends during the descent. The trip report describes both the route and the group's assistance.
takeaway: The outing's success included looking out for other people on the mountain, not only completing the planned route.
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph of a group walking together on a mountain trail
